lesson_title: Two Lessons, One Knife, No Blood
hook_text: Four learners, two lessons, one craft knife. Here is how the model gets built without a single plaster.
clip_script: Making day. Before anyone touches cardboard, two lists. The parts, counted and sized from the drawing, so nobody runs out. The order of work: cut everything, base, uprights, braces, axle, test. Everyone gets a job, because the bored learner is the one who gets cut. Now the knife. Mat underneath, steel ruler beside, cut away from you, fingers well back, light passes. Blade in when you stop. Wire: pliers and goggles, tape every sharp end. Glue gun: handle only, and cold water if it burns. Build the base, measure both diagonals, equal means square. Uprights, held with a set square. Braces. Push the top: no wobble. Holes opened till the dowel spins free, a card washer round each. Crank. Load it slowly, watch, fix, photograph. Two lessons, one knife, no blood, one working model.
visual_style: Whiteboard checklist ticks down; a knife on a mat against a ruler with a hand well back; a base rectangle with two equal diagonals; a frame rising stage by stage with a dowel spinning.
mood: Brisk workshop energy with a safety edge.
pacing: Plan, safety, build: three twenty-second blocks.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write your team's cutting list tonight.
